_comment: H-02 — certificate pinning coverage, derived from the host inventory.
The pin-set covered 2 of the 8 hosts the app talks to. That was not a
decision: the other six were hardcoded in src/utils/api.tsx (see H-01), so
whoever wrote the pin-set never saw them. Excluding Auth0 was a judgement
call; excluding the bank host was an omission, and from outside the file the
two looked identical.
This file is what makes them look different. Every host the app is configured
to reach must be either pinned in the Android pin-set or listed below with a
written reason and a review date. The release build fails otherwise — see the
H-02 coverage guard in android/app/build.gradle — and
__tests__/pinningCoverage.test.ts asserts the same invariant on every test run.
The inventory is read from the apiUrls block of environments/*.js and from any
baseURL literal left in src/. After H-01 there are no such literals.
TO PROMOTE A HOST FROM EXEMPT TO PINNED:
./scripts/compute-spki-pins.sh          (prints each chain and its SPKI hashes)
add a <domain-config> to android/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml
add the matching NSPinnedDomains entry to ios/exchangapay/Info.plist
delete the exemption below
The guards check that Android and iOS name the same hosts, so the platforms
cannot drift — unpinned hosts are materially more exposed on iOS, where ATS
still honours user-installed certificates.
M-03 — the single source of truth for pin-set expiry.
These dates were previously restated in five places: this file's prose,
the Android <pin-set expiration> attribute, the iOS Info.plist comment,
the iOS release build phase, and App.tsx. Five copies of a date that must
move together is a date that eventually moves in four places, and the one
that is missed fails silently in opposite directions — Android quietly
stops enforcing pinning, iOS keeps enforcing a pin that no longer matches.
Everything that can read JSON now reads it from here: App.tsx imports this
file, and the iOS build phase and the Gradle guard parse it. The two that
cannot read JSON — the Android XML attribute and the Info.plist comment —
are asserted against it by the Gradle guard and the iOS build phase, so
drift fails the build instead of shipping.
The keys are flat and uniquely named on purpose: a shell script and a
Gradle regex have to read them without a JSON parser, and a nested lookup
in sed is how a guard ends up silently matching nothing.
WHY THE TWO DATES DIFFER — this is not drift:
androidExpiration is deliberately EARLIER than the certificate's real
expiry. Android fails OPEN at this date, so it is a review deadline set
ahead of the cliff, chosen so the pin-set lapses into a build failure
while there is still time to act.
iosExpiration is the actual GeoTrust TLS RSA CA G1 expiry, because ATS
has no expiry of its own and fails CLOSED — once the pin stops matching,
the app cannot reach the API at all and the only remedy is an App Store
release. There is no fail-open margin to set, only a deadline to beat.
warnWithinDays drives the runtime Sentry signal in src/security/pinExpiry.ts.
buildWarnWithinDays drives the build-time warnings, and is larger because a
build is where the date can actually be changed.

findings: api.exchangapay.com and tstapi.exchangapay.com both chain through GeoTrust TLS RSA CA G1 (expires 2027-11-02), whose SPKI matches the primary pin in the pin-set exactly.
That intermediate is issued by DigiCert Global Root G2 (expires 2038-01-15), whose SPKI matches the backup pin exactly. The recovery path is real, not assumed.
The prod leaf expires 2026-12-13 and the tst leaf 2026-12-14. Neither is pinned, which is correct — renewal will not affect the pin-set.
The obsolete Azure, Suissebase and development hosts were removed from the mobile environment configuration on 2026-08-06.
Consequence for this file: every configured first-party API host is pinned on Android and iOS.

_comment: M-10 / pentest M-11 — Auth0 and Sumsub were exempt, leaving the Auth0 refresh
token and Sumsub KYC documents open to any rogue CA, and on iOS to any
user-installed CA profile. They are now pinned on both platforms.
ROOT level, not intermediate: Let's Encrypt (Auth0) and Google Trust Services
(Sumsub) pick from several intermediates at random, so an intermediate pin
would break login or KYC unannounced. A public root pin still rejects every
user-installed or rogue CA, which is the threat in the finding.
The set spans three CA families so a vendor CA switch stays inside it. If a
vendor moves to a CA outside this list, iOS login/KYC fails CLOSED until a
release — re-run ./scripts/compute-spki-pins.sh <host> at every reviewBy.

findings: exchangapay.eu.auth0.com and exchangapay-tst.eu.auth0.com: leaf CN=eu.auth0.com -> Let's Encrypt YE1 -> Root YE -> ISRG Root X2. Root YE and ISRG Root X2 SPKIs match the pins.
api.sumsub.com: leaf CN=sumsub.com -> GTS WE1 -> GTS Root R4. GTS Root R4 SPKI matches the pin.
The remaining root hashes were computed from the macOS system root store.

_comment: M-19 — only api.sumsub.com was pinned; whether the rest of the SDK's traffic
was covered had never been checked. Re-do this at every Sumsub SDK upgrade:
the host list below comes from the binaries, not from Sumsub's docs.
sdkNetworking.method: URL and TLS-API strings extracted from idensic-mobile-sdk-1.45.1.aar (classes.jar) and IdensicMobileSDK.xcframework/ios-arm64; live chains fetched with openssl s_client.

hosts.api.sumsub.com: REST API and the liveness websocket (wss://<baseUrl>/ws/liveness). Both platforms.
hosts.static.sumsub.com: CDN for SDK assets. Both platforms.
hosts.sentry.sumsub.com: The SDK's own bundled Sentry client (com.sumsub.sentry). Android only; pinned on iOS too so the platform parity guard holds.

sdkNetworking.notReached: dev-in.sumsub.com and test-api.sumsub.com appear in the SDK but are only used with withBaseUrl()/onTestEnv(); src/components/sumsub.tsx calls neither.
sdkNetworking.chains: All three hosts resolve to the same Cloudflare edge and serve the same CN=sumsub.com leaf -> GTS WE1 -> GTS Root R4. Covered by the existing GTS Root R4 pin; no new pin was needed.
sdkNetworking.android: Covered in full. The SDK ships no X509TrustManager, HostnameVerifier, CertificatePinner or custom SSLSocketFactory; it uses plain OkHttp (REST and websocket), which honours network_security_config.xml. No WebRTC native library is bundled, because videoident is not included.
sdkNetworking.ios: The REST API and the default websocket (SNSNativeWebSocket, URLSessionWebSocketTask) use URLSession, so ATS NSPinnedDomains applies.
residualRisk: iOS: the SDK also contains a legacy websocket (SNSLegacyWebSocket -> SNSJFRWebSocket, a vendored Jetfire fork on CFStreamCreatePairWithSocketToHost). CFStream is outside ATS, so NSPinnedDomains does NOT cover it, and it trusts user-installed CA profiles. Liveness frames would go over it if Sumsub turns on the server-side flag 'iosLegacyWebSockets'. Only Sumsub can set that flag. Ask them to confirm it is off for our client and stays off.
iOS: the SDK implements URLSession:didReceiveChallenge: and calls SecTrustEvaluate itself. ATS pinning should still be enforced before the delegate runs. Confirm on a device, not from this file.
sdkNetworking.runtimeCheck: On a test device, install a user CA (mitmproxy/Charles), route traffic through the proxy, and run a full KYC flow including liveness. Expected: every *.sumsub.com connection fails the TLS handshake on both platforms, and no *.sumsub.com host appears in the proxy log with decrypted content.

exemptions.reason: Third party, public data, and no credential ever reaches it — applyThirdPartyInterceptors in src/utils/apiInterceptors.ts withholds the bearer token and the device-risk header, asserted by __tests__/apiLayerHardening.test.ts. It currently chains through Google Trust Services WE1 / GTS Root R4, but CoinGecko can change CA without telling us, and an outage on the price screen buys no security: an attacker intercepting this can misstate a coin price and nothing else.
exemptions.remediation: None planned. Treat displayed prices as untrusted input.

exemptions.reason: This host appears only as an Auth0 audience identifier and is never resolved or contacted by the app. It should not be pinned.

Third-party operator, certificates rotate without notice. Bodies are allow-list redacted before they leave the device (C-07), so an interceptor gets shapes, not values.
